Ethernet

The RTL87x2G IC internally integrates an Ethernet peripheral, which is implemented through the GDMA controller for media access control at the MAC layer. Ethernet supports the Reduced Media Independent Interface (RMII) for connecting with an external PHY chip, and it also integrates a Station Management Interface (SMI) for communication with the external PHY.

LWIP is a lightweight open-source TCP/IP protocol stack that is widely used in low-end and mid-range controller platforms due to its open-source nature and low resource consumption. The RTL87x2G platform has been ported to the latest 2.1.3 version of LWIP.

Requirements

  1. RTL87x2G Model B EVB

  2. RTL8772GWP/RTL8772GWP-VI/RTL8772GWP-VM/RTL8772GWP-VA Daughterboard

  3. RTL8201FR: A 10/100Mbps Ethernet physical layer transceiver designed by Realtek that supports the RMII interface.

  1. ARM Keil MDK: https://developer.arm.com

  2. MP Tool: RealMCU

  3. Debug Analyzer: RealMCU

  4. Socket Test: https://sourceforge.net/projects/sockettest/

For more requirements, please refer to Quick Start .

Note

For detailed information about RTL8201FR, please contact the corresponding window of Realtek Ethernet PHY IC to obtain it.

Wiring

For the Ethernet module hardware on the EVB, refer to the B_Ethernet_Module in the Model B Evaluation Board.

The Ethernet interface pins are shown in the table below. The first 8 pins are for the RMII interface, while the last 2 pins are for the SMI interface. The pin assignment for the ETH interface is fixed and cannot be changed.

ETH Interface PINs

Name

PIN

Description

ETH_TX_EN

P10_1

Enable data transmission, the enable signal should be maintained at a valid level throughout the data transmission process.

ETH_TXD0

P10_0

RMII Transmit Data 0

ETH_TXD1

P9_7

RMII Transmit Data 1

ETH_CRS_DV

P9_5

RMII Carrier Sense and Data Valid

ETH_RXD0

P9_4

RMII Receive Data 0

ETH_RXD1

P9_3

RMII Receive Data 1

ETH_REF_CLK

P9_6

RMII Reference Clock. The internal clock source provides a 50 MHz reference clock.

ETH_RX_ERR

P10_2

Receive error signal

ETH_MDC

P1_7

SMI Management Data Clock

ETH_MDIO

P3_7

SMI Management Data I/O

Steps:

  1. Confirm that the RTL87x2G board is connected to the RTL8201FR PHY externally.

  2. Connect the Ethernet port of the RTL87x2G board to the router using an Ethernet cable.

  3. Connect the Ethernet port of the PC to the same router using an Ethernet cable.

  4. Disable all wireless networks on the PC to ensure that it is only using the wired Ethernet connection.

Building and Downloading

This sample can be found in the SDK folder:

Project file: samples\ethernet\ethernet\proj\mdk

Project file: samples\ethernet\ethernet\proj\gcc

To build and run the sample, follow the steps listed below:

  1. Open the project file.

  2. To build the target, follow the steps listed in the Generating App Image in Quick Start.

  3. After a successful compilation, the app_MP_xxx.bin will be generated in the directory sdk\samples\ethernet\ethernet\proj\mdk\bin.

  4. To download the app bin into EVB, follow the steps listed on the MP Tool Download in Quick Start.

  5. Press the reset button on the EVB board and it will start running.

Source Code Directory

  • Project directory: sdk\samples\ethernet\ethernet\proj

  • Source code directory: sdk\samples\ethernet\ethernet\src

Source files in the Ethernet application project are currently categorized into several groups as below.

└── Project: ethernet
    └── secure_only_app
        └── Device                   includes startup code
            ├── startup_rtl.c
            └── system_rtl.c
        ├── CMSIS                    includes CMSIS header files
        ├── CMSE Library             Non-secure callable lib
        ├── Lib                      includes all binary symbol files that user application is built on
        ├── Peripheral               includes all peripheral drivers and module code used by the application
        └── ethernet                 including Ethernet driver
            └── ethernet_driver.c
        ├── lwip/api                 includes LWIP TCP/IP source code
        ├── lwip/core                includes LWIP TCP/IP source code
        ├── lwip/netif               includes LWIP TCP/IP source code
        └── arch                     includes interface files for RTL87x2G and Ethernet
            ├── ethernetif.c         the file of Network card driver
            └── sys_arch.c           the file of LWIP OS Interface
        └── app                      includes the Ethernet user application implementation
            ├── main.c
            ├── common.c
            └── test.c

Typical Applications

TCP Server

RTL87x2G acts as a TCP server while the PC's SocketTest acts as the TCP client. Both sides establish a TCP connection, where RTL87x2G receives TCP data from the client and subsequently sends it back to the client.

Experimental Verification

  1. Run the program and check the firmware log to obtain the local IP address.

    [TCPIP_Init] local IP addr: 192.168.1.100

  2. On the SocketTest, open the Client tab and enter the local IP address into IP Address.

    Enter LOCAL_PORT in board.h into the Port.

  3. After resetting the EVB, click Connect.

  4. Enter the data to be sent, then click Send. Each time the data is sent, the received data column will display the sent data:

Code Overview

  1. Ethernet initialization. Achieved by calling eth_init_driver.

    1. The script definition is as follows:

    /*******************************************************
*                 ETHERNET Pin Config
*******************************************************/
#define ETH_TX_EN          P10_1
#define ETH_TXD0           P10_0
#define ETH_TXD1           P9_7
#define ETH_CRS_DV         P9_5
#define ETH_RXD0           P9_4
#define ETH_RXD1           P9_3
#define ETH_REF_CLK        P9_6
#define ETH_RX_ERR         P10_2
#define ETH_MDC            P1_7
#define ETH_MDIO           P3_7

    1. Call eth_init_pad_pinmux to configure PAD and PINMUX functions for pins.

    2. Call eth_init_data to initialize Ethernet data, mainly used to initialize TX/RX descriptors, buffer sizes, and storage locations.

    3. Modify the local MAC address through the MAC_ADDR1 - MAC_ADDR6 macros, ETH_SetMacAddr() is used to modify the MAC address.

    4. ETH_ClkInit() is used to initialize the Ethernet clock.

    5. eth_config_nvic is used to enable the NVIC interrupt.

    6. Call ETH_StructInit() to fill default values into ETH_InitTypeDef.

    7. In eth_init_driver(), modify the member variables in ETH_InitTypeDef as required:

      1. Sets the TX/RX descriptor number by calling ETH_SetDescNum().

      2. Sets the starting address of the TX/RX descriptor ring by calling ETH_SetDescAddr().

      3. Sets the starting address of the TX/RX descriptor data buffer by calling ETH_SetPktBuf().

      4. Sets the size of the TX/RX descriptor data buffer by calling ETH_SetBufSize().

      5. If there are other configuration requirements that need modification, add modifications to the ETH_InitTypeDef members.

    8. Initializes the Ethernet by calling ETH_Init().

  2. Creates an app task in main, app_main_task will call TCPIP_Init to initialize TCP/IP, and also create a test task by calling test_init. The main operations in test_thread are:

    1. Requests a TCP connection structure by calling netconn_new(NETCONN_TCP).

    2. Binds the local IP address and port number by calling netconn_bind(conn, IP_ADDR_ANY, LOCAL_PORT).

    3. Makes the TCP server enter the listening state by calling netconn_listen(conn).

    4. Handles client connection requests by calling netconn_accept(conn, &newconn).

    5. Receives data sent from the client by calling netconn_recv(newconn, &buf).

    6. Call netbuf_data(buf, &data, &len) to store the received data into data.

    7. Call netconn_write(newconn, data, len, NETCONN_COPY) to send the received data back to the client.

    8. Call netbuf_next(buf) to point to the next pbuf.

    9. Call netconn_close(newconn) to close the connection with the client.

    10. Call netconn_delete(newconn) to release the newconn space.

TCP Client

PC's SocketTest as the TCP server, Realtek RTL87x2G as the TCP client, both establish a TCP connection, and Realtek RTL87x2G sends data to the SocketTest.

Experimental Verification

  1. Retrieve the PC-side IPv4 address using ipconfig command.

  1. Fill in the PC-side IPv4 address at board.h in the DEST_IP_ADDR section.

    //dest ip addr
#define DEST_IP_ADDR0      192
#define DEST_IP_ADDR1      168
#define DEST_IP_ADDR2      1
#define DEST_IP_ADDR3      106

  2. On the SocketTest, open the Server tab.

    Fill in the PC-side IPv4 address at the IP Address field.

    Fill in the board.h DEST_PORT at the Port field.

  1. Click the Start Listening button and reset the EVB.

  2. The data reception field will display the sent data.

Code Overview

  1. Refer to Ethernet initialization .

  2. Creates an app task in main, app_main_task will call TCPIP_Init to initialize TCP/IP, and also create a test task by calling test_init. The main operations in test_thread are:

    1. Call netconn_new(NETCONN_TCP) to request a TCP connection structure.

    2. Call netconn_connect(conn, &ipaddr, DEST_PORT) to connect to the server.

    3. Call netconn_write(newconn, data, len, NETCONN_COPY) to send data to the server.

UDP

RTL87x2G and a PC's SocketTest communicate via UDP, where RTL87x2G receives UDP data and then sends it back to the SocketTest.

Experimental Verification

  1. Through ipconfig command to obtain the PC-side IPv4 address.

  1. Run the program and view the following log to obtain the local IP address.

    [TCPIP_Init] local IP addr: 192.168.1.100

  2. On the SocketTest, open the Udp tab.

    On the Server interface, fill in the PC-side IPv4 address in the IP Address column.

    On the Client interface, fill in the local IP address in the IP Address field, and fill in the LOCAL_PORT in board.h in the Port field.

  1. After resetting the EVB, click Start Listening button.

  2. Enter the data to be sent, then click Send Data button. After each transmission, the data bar received will display the sent data.

Code Overview

  1. Refer to Ethernet initialization .

  2. Creates an app task in main, app_main_task will call TCPIP_Init to initialize TCP/IP, and also create a test task by calling test_init. The main operations in test_thread are:

    1. Call netconn_new(NETCONN_UDP) to request a UDP connection structure.

    2. Call netconn_bind(conn, IP_ADDR_ANY, LOCAL_PORT) to bind the local IP address and port number.

    3. Call netconn_recv(newconn, &buf) to receive data from the client.

    4. Call netbuf_copy(buf, buffer, sizeof(buffer)) to save the received data into the buffer.

    5. Call netconn_send(conn, buf) to send the received data back to the client.

Jperf RX

RTL87x2G as the TCP server, PC terminal Jperf upper machine as the TCP client, both establish a TCP connection. The PC terminal Jperf upper machine sends data, and the RTL87x2G terminal TCP server receives the data.

Experimental Verification

  1. Run the program and check the following log to obtain the local IP address.

    [TCPIP_Init] local IP addr:192.168.1.100

  2. In the PC terminal Jperf upper machine, fill in the local IP address in the Server address field.

    Fill LOCAL_PORT in board.h with Client Port field.

  1. After duplicating the EVB, click the Run Iperf button.

  2. The upper machine on the PC end Jperf will display real-time speed.

Note

The process log output will be closed during speed testing.

Code Overview

  1. Reference Ethernet initialization .

  2. Creates an app task in main, app_main_task will call TCPIP_Init to initialize TCP/IP, and also create a test task by calling test_init. The main operations in test_thread are:

    1. Call netconn_new(NETCONN_TCP) to request a TCP connection structure.

    2. Call netconn_bind(conn, IP_ADDR_ANY, LOCAL_PORT) to bind the local IP address and port number.

    3. Call netconn_listen(conn) to make the TCP server enter the listening state.

    4. Call netconn_accept(conn, &newconn) to handle client connection requests.

    5. Call netconn_recv(newconn, &buf) to receive data sent by the client.

    6. Call netbuf_data(buf, &data, &len) to save the received data into data.

    7. Call netbuf_next(buf) to point to the next pbuf.

    8. Call netconn_close(newconn) to close the connection with the client.

    9. Call netconn_delete(newconn) to release the space occupied by newconn.

Jperf TX

Realtek RTL87x2G serves as the TCP client, PC-side Jperf host serves as the TCP server, both establish a TCP connection, and RTL87x2G sends data to the PC-side Jperf host.

Experimental Verification

  1. Obtain the PC-side IPv4 address using the ipconfig command.

  1. Fill in the PC-side IPv4 address in the DEST_IP_ADDR section of board.h.

    //dest ip addr
#define DEST_IP_ADDR0      192
#define DEST_IP_ADDR1      168
#define DEST_IP_ADDR2      1
#define DEST_IP_ADDR3      106

  2. In the PC-side Jperf host, fill in DEST_PORT from board.h into the Listen Port field.

  1. Click the Run Iperf button to reorient the EVB.

  2. The real-time speed will be displayed on the PC-end Jperf client.

Note

The engineering log output will be closed during the speed test.

Code Overview

  1. Refer to Ethernet initialization .

  2. Creates an app task in main, app_main_task will call TCPIP_Init to initialize TCP/IP, and also create a test task by calling test_init. The main operations in test_thread are:

    1. Call netconn_new(NETCONN_TCP) to request a TCP connection structure.

    2. Call netconn_connect(conn, &ipaddr, DEST_PORT) to connect to the server.

    3. Call netconn_write(conn, send_buf, IPERF_BUFSZ, NETCONN_COPY) to send data to the server.
